The build materials and design are outstanding. Big Agnes has designed the fabric to be more durable in the wear areas, while shaving weight elsewhere. The seat width is also perfectly comfortable. Comes with a little bag that easily allows the chair to be packed. If there's one negative, it comes in the price. Those that hike, though, can understand quality, weight, and price are areas that have give and take. You get a great quality item that's generally lightweight (ultralight packers won't have a chair anyways, but for those like myself that appreciate a couple comforts this is quite manageable) but you're going to spend a few bucks on it.

It's traveled on two hike trips with me thus far and I've enjoyed pulling it up near the campfire at night. I'd gladly purchase this chair again in a heartbeat.

HYDRONICA Waterproof Backpack Wet/Dry Bag 30L 8 Gallon with Enhanced Shoulder Straps. (Black) Because of the near perfect customer reviews for this bag I gave it a shot. After getting our stuff stolen off the beach in Waikiki a few years ago I never leave anything on the beach anymore. I purchased this bag for an 8 day trip to Maui. For the most part I used it just as a backpack and left it on the beach while someone always stayed back to watch our gear. Kind of sucked that our full group of 5 could not enjoy the water together so on the final 2 days of our trip I took it into the ocean with us. The bag was never completely underwater. I would just let the bag float within an arm's reach near me.

After getting back to the beach and taking my gear out I saw water all over the inside of the bag. Yes, I was careful and folded the top at least 5 times before closing the clasp. I now have two ruined iPhone 6 pluses and a Panasonic point and shoot camera. I'm wondering if I just got a lemon.

This morning I tried the sink test. Dropped some hats into the bag, filled up the kitchen sink, tossed the bag around a bit, and gave the bag a good squeeze. I could see air bubbles immediately. If air bubbles are coming out that means water is getting in. This bag is certainly getting returned. Now I'm wondering who should be responsible for my damaged electronics.
text_fidelity_b: HYDRONICA Waterproof Backpack Wet/Dry Bag 30L 8 Gallon with Enhanced Shoulder Straps. (Black)

text_fidelity_a: Graber 4 Bike Hitch Rack In the past, our family has used a bike rake that fits onto the trunk of the car. The kind with tons of straps and buckles. However, our newest truck (a Toyota 4Runner) has a towing hitch, so I selected this Graber Bike Hitch for ease and convenience. My husband was able to assemble the rack in a short period of time (about 30 minutes), but was stalled when he noticed that some of the parts (the Cotter pin and some bolts) were missing from the package. I contacted Graber customer service and within days had the replacement parts. Fabulous customer service by the way.). Once the parts arrived, he was able to securely attach the rack to the vehicle. The rack appears to be well-made and sturdy. There are straps to attach the bike(s) to the rack.  The rack is black, matches the vehicle and can hold up to four bikes, which is great since we are a four-member family. We have three Diamond Backs and an Access Stealth 4.0. Our bikes range is weight, with the Access being the lightest since it has a full graphite body. Two things I think most bike lovers will appreciate about the Graber: (1) you can lower the apparatus to the ground by removing the metal pins and easily remove bikes and (2) by removing the top pin, you can lower the arm when the rack is not in use. And finally, the Graber is reasonably priced (under $150).  Overall, I am pleased and would recommend this product. 4 stars
text_fidelity_b: Graber 4 Bike Hitch Rack

text_fidelity_a:
Trudeau Mist 19-Ounce Hydrator Bottle, Breast Cancer Research Foundation Pink I got these hydrators in all four colors, and they are mostly pretty good - but don't last forever. One of the misters was always hard to pump, one mister quit working after about six months, and the dogs chewed the spray-top off a third. After a while, the deployable straw in two of the hydrators started catching inside the bottle top when rotated, but it's not difficult to winkle it out. One does leak a bit, but so do a lot of sports bottles I've encountered. After a while, two started squeaking when water was drawn through the straw.

So they could be better, but right now I don't see anything better out there. They look cool and are the bomb for preventing spills. They are perfect bedside bottles for a guy like me who tosses and turns a bit, and while the mister holds out they have a thousand and one uses. We've used the mister to mist plants, clean glass, and discipline the dogs, though the aforesaid has resulted. Note that while the deployable straw is 1/4" in diameter, the inner straw is smaller, so the hydrator is fluids only - no smoothies or anything like that. It's easy to drop ice in, though.

Handwashing is best. I do occasionally run them through the dishwasher (top shelf,) but that doesn't really clean the deployable straws, which have to be disassembled to be properly cleaned. Gunk seems to build up at the top of the inner straw over time. After removing the cap, you must push the deployable straw down while gently wiggling down the inner straw - once the latter comes off, grasp the base of the deployable straw and pull it out all the way. Putting it back is a little tricky; insert the deployable straw first and push it all the way in, then push the inner straw into it with the diagonal end pointed to the bottom of the bottle. Sometimes you have to adjust the diagonal end so it doesn't lay flat on the bottom.

If they were just a LITTLE more reliable (or cheaper,) I'd have to give them five stars. If anyone knows of anything better with these features, let me know!
text_fidelity_b: Trudeau Mist 19-Ounce Hydrator Bottle, Breast Cancer Research Foundation Pink

text_fidelity_a: NFL Remote Phone Charger These phone chargers are good item to have as a backup in an emergency, but you will need to make sure it is charged before you really need it. It comes with a retractable charging cord. Another good feature, is that it has 2 USB ports so you could charge to devices at once. It took about 4 hours to charge when plugged into the wall, and slightly longer when I used the computer. After the first charge the football seems to charge up faster. There is a light that will stay red when it is still charging and then it will eventually turn blue when it is finished. You need to make sure you hit the small button in the middle to turn it on. When you are using the football to charge the red light will flash to let you know the power is low and it is about to stop charging your phone/device. I was able to charge an iPhone from 6% to 100% and then a Samsung galaxy from 0% to 68% all in one football charge. It charges at a rate of about 2% per minute. I really like that it charges your phone very fast, but I was hoping to get two full phone charges out of one single football charge. The speed makes up for it, so I am pleased.  Made in China.

XMark 11-Gauge Our bench arrived from the manufacturer in great condition, and my husband had it set up within an hour. It's a much nicer bench than others we've owned in this price range or below. It's stable, the foam isn't too soft so it won't bottom out, the ladder back is so easy to use, as is the seat adjustment. We're very happy with the seat positions, including the upright and flat positions.

There's no rattles or issues, the cushions are well made and stitching is very nice, and the bench, while heavier duty than some we've owned, is still light enough to be moved by one person - oh, partly because the wheels are good quality. The seat back is a little wider than some, like the Hoist HF-4165 (an awesome bench, btw) and that works well for us.

The only thing I don't love about it is the angle of the foot hold down, which for my taste is too close to the bench for comfort. It's pretty adjustable, though - you can turn the hold down attachment upside down if you want a little more distance from the bench. And yes, there's a gap between the seat and the seat back when the bench is flat, but that's normal since the seat is so thick. You can always buy a piece of foam and cut out a piece to use when the bench is flat if it's a problem. BTW, I'd consider it light commercial, not commercial - but since there will only be 2 of us using it, that's more than fine.

We've owned a number of benches, and this one is the keeper for us as it puts everything we're looking for together in one bench. Great for sit-ups, including declines, and very nice for a wide variety of exercises. I don't mean to sound like a broken record, but I really love this bench!

text_fidelity_a:
Taylor Made Products StepSafe Dock Steps I already had the single version of this exact dock step, used on my own wood dock. The dock is old and weathered and therefore not slippery. Having recently purchased a sailboat docked at a marina in a rented slip, I thought it would be perfect.
I learned 2 things. First of all, size matters. If it's too much of a stretch, you don't center your weight on the step. That means that when your leg is extended, it can push the step away from you. Result? SPLASH!
Secondly, consider the dock texture. The rental, unlike my dock, is smooth. If you have the right size for the boat, slipping isn't as much of an issue because your weight will be more evenly distributed, but if the dock itself is slick, of course it's an increased risk.

So, while I would have rather used what I already have, getting this one, which is a perfect size, was a good investment.
I was quite surprised to learn that I'm allowed to drill holes in the rented dock, so for 100% safety (and because I'm a klutz) it's going to be bolted down. That's also a good idea because nothing is as annoying as waking up after a storm to find that your steps jumped ship!
I hope this review helps, if you need more info or a photo, I'm happy to oblige

UPDATE: I added the [[ASIN:B001448T72 Taylormade Dock Step Railing Double Tread]], for increased safety. Easy to install, very pleased with both purchases.
text_fidelity_b: Taylor Made Products StepSafe Dock Steps

Bike Lights for Night Riding, USB Rechargeable Shark 500 Ultra Bright LED Bike Light Front and Back Safety Tail Light Included, Bicycle Light Compatible with Mountain, Road, Kids & City Bicycles I have been using the review sample that I received for about six weeks. I took my time because some reviews cited the mount as a weak link as well as disputing whether or not this is the 'brightest'. I will admit that the mount seems flimsy, but in six weeks of relatively hard use it has held up.

As for brightness, I cannot say that it is or isn't the brightest. I will say that it illuminates a narrow path in front of you and definitely is oncoming driver friendly.

One thing about the mount is it will snap the light in place and firmly hold it if you follow the instruction sheet. It also quick releases the light so it will not get stolen when you chain your bike and go shopping or whatever. Plus it, like the tail light, installs without tools. I love that feature. I also love the fact that this light charges using a standard USB cable and not some proprietary one with a barrel connector. That is one of the reasons why I awarded this five stars.

Since the product specs cover the use and charging times in depth, I will not recite them here. I will say that I run mine at 100% brightness all the time and the 1.5 hour use time is fairly accurate.

There may be better lights on the market, but not at this one's price. I am thoroughly pleased with it and happy that I gave it six weeks before rushing to review it. In my opinion there is nothing seriously wrong with it and a lot that is right.
text_fidelity_b: Bike Lights for Night Riding, USB Rechargeable Shark 500 Ultra Bright LED Bike Light Front and Back Safety Tail Light Included, Bicycle Light Compatible with Mountain, Road, Kids & City Bicycles

I have lupus, good days and bad days. Some days, I barely make it up the stairs. Some days, I can do all right. But no matter what, if I have a flare or get an infection or whatever, I decondition really rapidly. The saving grace has been that I worked with horses for the entire first part of my adult life, so my baseline leg strength was high.

Resistance bands are the major component of my maintenance exercise. You can use them in bed, on the couch, wherever your body is, whatever it can do. BUT it is really difficult to work inner thighs just with resistance bands - especially without standing up.

Enter Thigh Master.

This isn't the old giant thing we saw on the Three's Company lady's infomercials, but it works on the same principle. It's a resistance device. Super easy to set up, and durable - at least for an old lady. And I am regaining some hip strength in addition to working some old muscles that desperately needed it.

100% recommend, especially for people who may need to exercise in a bed or on a chair or wherever their bodies will allow them to be - and I will leave you with the immortal words of the late great Jan Hooks: They say you can use it anywhere, so there I was, using my thigh master in the laundromat... Penn International VIS 2 Speed Reel, Gold, 30 What a great reel for big, powerful fish! If you target fish that measure in the hundreds of pounds, and you want the best tool for the job, this is your reel. In my case, it's the reel I use when we go deep for big halibut here in Alaska. This reel holds plenty of line to get to those shelves 400 feet down where the barndoors lie, with plenty of line left over to allow for long runs that those big fish make. If you hang up and break off, losing several hundred feet of line (it happens), you don't have to hang it up because the reel holds enough line to let you keep fishing.

I like the high-speed retrieve for pulling up from the deep when you need to check your bait or try something else. When you latch into a fish, though, a quick push of the button on the hub of the handle engages the more powerful lower gears, so you can really torque into the fish.

That new handle design is nice, too. It comfortably fits my hand, has a nice rubbery, no-slip texture, and helps spread the stress across the meaty part of my hand so long battles are just a little bit easier.

The open design of the "X" series frame (with no crossbars across the front of the spool) is helpful when there's a backlash to deal with (yeah, it still happens once in a while). These reels aren't cheap, but they're the best you can buy. Solid, reliable, and made in USA. No regrets here!

Let me know if you don't anything in my review helpful.
text_fidelity_b: Penn International VIS 2 Speed Reel, Gold, 30

Intex Excursion Pro Kayak Series I bought this kayak a year ago, and have used it close to 30 times. I have used it as a tandem kayak and as a fishing kayak (not simultaneously - that would be a tight squeeze). It has survived rocky rivers with low water, dozens of fishing trips, and being dragged up boat ramps. I am really impressed with the durability. Also, it fits in the trunk of my Toyota Corolla. Awesome! My only complaint is that the inflatable seats aren't very comfortable for long outings. Also, Amazon is WAY overpriced for this product. When I bought mine, I found it elsewhere for 30% less (still new!). I definitely recommend looking around online before buying here. A good price is closer to $200.

Year 2 update:

The inflatable seats were the first thing to go. Both seats only hold air for a few hours now. They are made out of a much cheaper material than the rest of the kayak, so I guess that was to be expected. I also got my first puncture on one of the pontoons. I used the patching kit and recommended adhesive, but the patch keeps coming off. I think it is because it falls along a natural crease when the kayak is deflated. That constant bending puts a lot of stress on the patch. It's annoying to keep re-patching it, but it does at least hold air while the patch is on.
text_fidelity_b: Intex Excursion Pro Kayak Series

The tension increases as you compress the buttons. The further you press the harder you have to press. I can't see any mechanism to adjust the tension as you can with the FA-10P model. I recommend substituting bungee strap in place of the latex strap provided - it is easier to adjust and gives better tension. Actually, once properly adjusted, the soft frame feels quite comfortable and, even after wearing them for about 35 minutes, they cause less eye pain than the usual "orbit" goggles. Nonetheless, I would not recommend these for "occasional" and inexperienced swimmers. Be extremely careful not to get hit in the face while wearing these.
I agree that they fog up quickly. This seems to be a chronic problem: every goggles I've owned fog up. You can solve the problem by using a defogger (I love Cressi anti-fog spray which I use when I go scuba diving) or, just use a bit of spit and rub it in - cheap and effective. CamelBak Men's Palisade Hike Hydration Pack - Integrated Rain Cover Camelback rarely disappoints and the quality of this bag is no exception. The back of it is soft and supportive against your back while offering comfort and air-flow that does not diminish when the bag and 3-liter bladder are full. The bag is durable and sturdy, with soft lining on some inner pockets for things like a cell phone, GPS, or satellite link. Inside there are larger compartments with a couple of smaller ones, and snack pockets on the waist-band (at least that's what I use them for!). There is also a built-in pocket for the rain shield so you won't lose it, as well as clips for your poles. We were even able to fit a small tent in the stash pocket! I never would have guessed the bag could have that capacity going by looks alone.

However, there are a couple of things I wish I could change about the bag. The water compartment is pretty big, it cuts into pack space more than I'd like when it's full. There also aren't many clips and loops on the outside beyond the pole clips. Not spaces for carabiners etc. Dirty shoes, dog bowls, they all have to go IN the pack.

text_fidelity_a:
SCHWINN Fitness 230 Recumbent Bike Wow! This bike has all the bells and whistles and is comfortable, too! While recumbent bikes aren't as good an overall workout as elliptical machines or upright bikes (since you're sitting), they are still low-impact and can help with the lower half of the body, as well as provide some cardio.

I'll go item by item, since there are so many noteworthy features:

**Ease of Assembly: 5 stars
The manual covered everything, and while it took some time to put together, everything went smoothly and came out perfectly. Not difficult, and it took well under two hours. I am female and assembled it with no help, so don't worry about anything being too heavy...as long as you don't try moving the box. (The delivery guys were more than happy to bring the box inside, earning them an unsolicited tip, but if that's not the case for you, just open the box and bring the parts in individually. No big deal.)

**Features and Settings: 5 stars
You can enter user data with age, height, and gender, to get better and more accurate results. Combined with sensors that let you see your heart rate, you can see what sort of activity you are doing (cardiovascular, fat burning, etc.), and unlike with some other machines, the heart rate sensor worked fine. Other features included different pre-programmed settings like workouts with alternating difficulties in patterns set to any time or level you like.

**Extras: 5 stars
There is a USB port to charge your mobile or tablet device!! You can also plug into the auxiliary port to use the speakers and play music--it even comes with the cable needed! The speakers are pretty loud and clear for something like this, so it's a great add-on! There is also a three-setting fan that works well when you get hot.

**Overall workout: 5 stars
The smooth movement and comfortable seating with air holes to allow your skin to breathe, along with so many extra features, make this an excellent workout tool, with the quality you would expect from a good gym. I LOVE this machine!

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Flex Wireless Activity + Sleep Wristband, Black, Pedometer, Small/Large I've had my Fitbit Flex for about a week. At first, I was fairly impressed when I actually counted my steps and compared it to the Fitbit calculations. However, it can be very quirky and inaccurate under certain circumstances. I have mine on my right wrist, and I am right-handed, so I made sure to set it to the "Dominant" wrist setting. But, to get truly accurate readings, your arm really needs to be at your side. If I'm carrying things around the house, I don't get an accurate count. If I'm walking through the store, pushing a grocery cart, I don't get an accurate count. It seriously under counts my steps. I'd like to send it back and exchange it for the Fitbit One, which I have since heard is more accurate. However, I didn't realize that Amazon only takes returns on unopened items, and otherwise charges a restocking fee. And, I'm not sure this is defective. I think it's just not accurate. Should have bought this from a Brick & Mortar store.

Edited 4/1/2014...Ok, I've been using my Fitbit for a few more days. Today I was out for several hours and my step count was still really low as, described previously, I don't walk with my hands down at my side. I'm usually busy doing other things. I had contacted Fitbit regarding the problem, but the only thing they could say was that it compared to other wrist-trackers on the market....which isn't saying a lot. I'd really like to return or exchange this thing, but can't. When I got home this afternoon, and saw that my step count was again very low, I decided to try taking the Flex unit out of the wrist band and I put it in my pocket. So far, that seems to give me a better step count. Not sure how it will work that way with the other functions. But, frankly, after using the Flex for over a week, I'm not confident in the accuracy of the other functions and will probably never use them. There is an Omron brand clip-on that gets rave reviews. Check that one out before you decide to buy the Flex.

Edited 4/3/2014...I pursued my issues with Fitbit customer service, and this is what they said: " Flex will count your steps when you're walking with your arms stationary, as we do want to give you credit for this activity. This includes walking while pushing a stroller or shopping cart, or holding on to a treadmill. However, because your hands are not moving, your step count may be a bit lower during this activity."

So, they have finally admitted the count is not accurate unless your arms are down at your side. I do dispute the fact that it is a "bit lower." My steps are hardly being counted at all, unless my arm is down at my side. So, for this reason, I have now lowered my rating to two stars. I did contact Amazon customer service and explained what was going on. They are allowing me to return it, without restocking charges, because it is not working as intended. THANKS AMAZON!!!
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Flex Wireless Activity + Sleep Wristband, Black, Pedometer, Small/Large

text_fidelity_a:
Planet Bike Grunge Board downtube bike fender I've got a bicycle without any mounting holes for fenders. It also doesn't have enough clearance between the forks/brakes and tires to jerry-rig a fender. However, I hate not riding my bike because of light rain or a few puddles.

The Grunge Board was the best option that I could find at a reasonable price. It straps onto the downtube with a couple of rubber straps. I've got an 80s racing bike with tight geometry, and the dimensions of the board are small enough to clear the crankarms and the front wheel during turns. But just so (orientation makes a difference).

I've ridden through some big puddles and it seems to do a fairly good job of keeping my pant legs from getting soaked. I still put some scotch tape over the holes/slits around the bottom bracket to keep the gunk from getting in. The board is light enough that I leave it on all the time, even when it's not raining...just in case there is an unexpected puddle.

I have to take off a star because I think the mounting band should have been designed better. First, it hard to push the rubber bands through the narrow slots once they wrap around the downtube. The bands have slits in them that attach to nubs on the underside of the board. The nubs are not large enough to hold the bands in place perfectly securely. They seem to usually work, but the bands come off occasionally. If you have a small diameter downtube (as in most pre-90s, bikes), there are also a couple inches of extra rubber band that just flop around. It shouldn't be too hard for Planet Bike to redesign this retention mechanism, but it's also hard to complain for ~$10.

You can use a couple of cable ties instead of the rubber bands and they'd probably do a better job. You could also use a large soda bottle cut to size and get the same effect, though arguably a bit uglier.
text_fidelity_b: Planet Bike Grunge Board downtube bike fender

text_fidelity_a:
GymPaws Real Leather Hand Pad Workout Glove Alternative | Hygienic n' Washable | Slightly Padded Palm w 4 Finger Loop SweatProof Back | Mens | Womens I gave up gloves about 10 years ago in favor of pads/grips. It felt odd at first, but after a few weeks, I realized that I could never go back to using gloves. Gloves were bulky, bunched in the wrong places, and made my hands too sweaty and hot. Pads/grips gave me protection without adding bulk, were easy to take on and off when necessary, and held up longer. The only thing I didn't like was that they had a single strap that went across the back of the hand. Even if I laced my fingers through the strap, I could never get a firm enough hold to keep them on for things like medicine ball work. Everything else -- dumbbells, barbells, rowing, push ups -- was fine. So when I lost those grips, I ordered GymPaws because I thought that the individual finger loops would make for a solid grip.

Unfortunately, the GymPaws weren't a good fit for me. On three of the four finger loops, I could see daylight between my fingers and the material -- not a lot but enough that I felt the pads sliding when trying to do some fast work with the medicine ball. So GymPaws were too big for my fingers, yet they were also too small for my palms. I'm a woman, about 5'2", and my hands are proportional to my size, though obviously smaller than many other people's hands. The brand I used before GymPaws provided more coverage on the palm, but the GymPaws left a bit too much skin exposed at the base of my thumb. It didn't prevent me from getting a solid grip on the dumbbells, barbell, or rower, but it was often irritating.

Making a product like this has got to be difficult because you can only make so many sizes and still keep the price affordable. Having one size only is the easiest way, but then it's, 'One size fits all, some better than others.' For something like this, I think the only way to know is to order them and try them out for yourself.

Although I didn't like the product, I've got nothing but praise for their customer service. The return window is only 14 days, but you can return them even if they've been used. That's exactly what I did and I got my refund as soon as they received the package. Given that, I'd say that it's worth giving GymPaws a try. They didn't work for me, but they seem to work for a lot of people. Although I only had them a short time, they felt sturdy and well-made enough to last a while. But try them on every sort of gear you regularly use before the return window shuts, especially if you're transitioning from regular gloves.
text_fidelity_b: GymPaws Real Leather Hand Pad Workout Glove Alternative | Hygienic n' Washable | Slightly Padded Palm w 4 Finger Loop SweatProof Back | Mens | Womens

I needed something at least that size or bigger and that proved more difficult than expected. I had no idea my pack would be considered so large, it barely fit everything I needed as it is! I only gave it 4 stars because it has only a very small pouch for school supplies. While I understand that it isn't necessarily built for a student, it does have a pouch for a laptop so I guess I assumed it would be more business/student friendly.

In any case, it's large enough but that space is much taller than it is wide. So far, it seems to fit everything I need. I put 2 medium sized text books, 2 spiral bound single subject notebooks, a novel sized book, a 13'' mac in the laptop sleeve and a spiral bound textbook with room to spare. Empty, it's much lighter than my JanSport pack which I appreciate.

It seems to be very well made but I wish it had some of the features of their other packs like the pockets on the waist strap or shoulder straps. It'd be nice to have my phone in front of me instead of in the pack itself but I guess that's what pockets are for. There are 2 stretchy water bottle pockets that seem to accommodate large bottles but they are hard to reach and impossible to put back without taking the pack off. At least that's what I've found out carrying a 1 liter sized bottle today.

The color is gorgeous! I love, love, LOVE it! It's a very deep aqua/turquoise color that's not overly bright or obnoxious. It's seriously one of the nicest looking packs I found in this price range when shopping and I looked at everyone and I mean EVERYONE! I spent about 2 days doing research and this was one of the best deals for the most volume out there. Overall, I think most students would be happy with it but it might be considered very large if you don't pack your books around all day. I carpool so I get dropped off at school in the morning and don't leave until early evening. I need to take all my books, workout clothes, food etc... So this pack still might be a little tight for all that but we'll see.

UPDATED 08/28/14

The bag has held up extremely well. I questioned how the elastic pockets on the front and sides would hold up and they seem to be just fine. After having it for a year I have to say the shape is frustrating. It's too tall and narrow so it wastes too much space. R Value of 4.9 - Inflatable Camping Mattress I do a lot of camping of all kinds and have had many pads over the years, from expensive brand name ones to $10 foam pads from a gas station in the middle of nowhere.

Don't buy this if you think it's the same thing as a brand name pad at less than half the cost. It does well, but has some significant disadvantages. Read on for more detail.

Successfully imitates the more expensive pads in:
* Comfort - it's thick and it's soft.
* Warmth - it's thickness and foaminess insulates decently well.
* Durability - time will tell, but it appears to be made of a thick sturdy material.

Here is where this pad falls short:
* It's big and heavy when compressed. Almost twice the size of the brand name pads. I'd think twice about using this for backpacking if you plan on going far or fast.
* The valve sucks. Most good pads have a valve that can be close by snapping it in, this one will let air out while you spin it shut.
* The foam/insulation is cheap - meaning it's not as warm as a comparable pad of the same weight. Probably fine down to freezing temps though.
* The material is very plasticky and doesn't have a very pleasant feel to it. I know this is nitpicking, but you're going to be sleeping on this after all, it should be pleasant.

text_fidelity_a:
KastKing World's Premier Copolymer Fishing Line Great Upgrade For Monofilament Fishing Line Substitute For Fluorocarbon Fishing Line I have been a nylon monofilament guy for years. I tried Spiderwire as an experiment and truly hated it and quickly went back to mono, happy and content with it. I was not familiar with copolymer line and was provided some for testing. It has changed my opinion of mono.

The biggest issue I have had with mono is that it is prone to memory (retaining the coil from the spindle on which it is spooled). Cast out and you get a plastic spring on the water. It doesn’t really hurt anything until you try to reel it in quickly with no load, and then you get a “rat’s nest” on the spool. I have not had this line long enough to tell if this is going to be a problem, but I have seen some other benefits.

Compared to the same lb-test line, this copolymer line is slightly more limber and flexible. I never realized that monofilament is actually somewhat stiff - well, it’s stiff in comparison to the copolymer line, anyway.

Something else I noticed about this line is that it is less likely to kink and snag in use. Monofilament has a bad tendency to get cuts and abrasions in it and I always assumed this was just part of the price one pays for the pleasure of fishing. I was startled to find that this doesn’t have to be the case. As a test I grabbed a phillips screwdriver and pressed the bit of it at an angle against a strand of monofilament line and made an indentation. I did the same to the copolymer line and was surprised that the copolymer did not retain any misshapenness and did not show any signs of cuts. The monofilament showed a very small imperfection in the line where I pressed the screwdriver. Cuts in a line, even small ones, are often the difference between a catch and losing a good fish, and I am encouraged by the copolymer’s ability to be a little more resistant to damage.

I have the green copolymer and it blends in nicely into the water.

In casting the copolymer line peels off the reel very smoothly and with a good reel I get excellent casting distance. I don’t see too much difference between the copolymer and the monofilament when casting.

I never considered anything other than monofilament before now. Copolymer line is new to me and so far it seems to be a little better than nylon monofilament. KastKing’s line is competitively priced too compared to other brands and it seems to be a good product. I have no basis to compare against other copolymer brands, but I will be gradually switching over to it and right now I’m happy with this brand’s performance.

Disclaimer: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.
text_fidelity_b: KastKing World's Premier Copolymer Fishing Line Great Upgrade For Monofilament Fishing Line Substitute For Fluorocarbon Fishing Line

DESIGN: this is made to not only install with no tools, but to also be water- and dust-proof. Apparently the engineers know a thing or two about riding bicycles in all kinds of terrain. The nicest feature in my opinion is this set is portable. You can easily switch it from one bike to another by unhooking it. Of course, that makes it a target for theft so this is best removed when you have your bike parked in populated or uncontrolled areas.

The fast and slow flash modes, and the steady light are switchable by depressing the lens for each mode, plus off. The two flashing modes work on both the white and red lights, and the fast flash has a strobe effect that makes for excellent safety. That, plus the two hundred forty degree illumination make bikes highly visible at night.

The band which you hook around handle bars or seat posts is made of silicon and is practically indestructible. It will adjust to very small diameters (in fact I have it on a microphone stand at the moment.)

Bottom line: this is one of the safest products a bike rider can own. If you own more than one bike it can quickly and easily moved from one to another, so you need only invest in a single set.

text_fidelity_a:
Horizon Fitness T101 Treadmill I researched the hell out of treadmill before buying this one looking at costco, sams club, amazon, sears, etc and reading product reviews all over the internet. What sold me on this the most was the east of assembly and the sturdyness. My husband is 6'-2 and 300lbs. This has a 300lb deck and we have had no problems. Also what this offered over other models in the same class was 2" more of deck, a beafier motor and longer warrranty...all big pluses when you live in a rural area. A pleasant surprise on this model that wasnt listed was a cooling fan feature with three settings to at least move the air around your face when you get that heart pumping and a little sweat rolling down.
This is a fold up model, but I would like it more if folded up a full 90 degrees, but even at an angle, this has one of the highest angles that I've seen, folding at about at 65-70 degree angle...very much out of the way.
The thing is loaded with features, one which is nice is a VERY slow speed....1/2 mph...which for my extended family, is what my sneior father recovering from his second round of CHF needs. He know he needs to walk and has tried other friends treadmills, but they don't go slow enough...usually only .7 of .8 mph. The .5 mph in his exhaustive, delicate state is perfect to start and move him up to .7 and .8 mph for 5-6 minutes. Doesn't sound like much, but when your old and recovering, its alot. He's already seen an improvement in his endurance. On the other end of the spectrum, I like to move that incline all the way up to 10% and move out at 3 mph for 20 minutes (this is when the fan feels really nice, as does being able to plug in your ipod or mp3 player) and then back down to 2-3% grade for 10-15 minute cool down. Even my daughter is liking a treadmill.
I took us about 35-40 minutes to assemble...including unpacking from the box.
Delivery was great, though, because I am rural, I package actually arrived in Reno from the shipper within a few days, but then I had to way 3 weeks for the "truck" to have "a load" to head out into the rural areas for a delivery run. But when it did arrive, the driver moved it right into the garage for us (which sits 150 feet from the street). So 5 stars for the driver.
I can't really find anything that this treadmill doesn't do. I tend to buy things that fall somewhere in the middle when it comes to customer reviews, but a few things...like appliances, TVs and this treadmill, I wanted to get as much bang for my buck as I could. Yes, I would love to have the money to buy a Solei or other high end model, but for my family needs, my budget, the durability that it must stand up to, I am extremely pleased.
text_fidelity_b: Horizon Fitness T101 Treadmill

text_fidelity_a: Stanley GO The Quick Flip GO Bottle 24OZ Glass We have now owned several of these water bottles, as they are a really great size, and we enjoy the flip top feature; however, before purchasing, please know that the plastic lid has a weak point that will break if dropped on basically any surface at all.  While we try very hard not to drop our water bottles, accidents occasionally happen, and the lids of two of our water bottles are now broken.  I was hopeful that I could find replacement lids either on Amazon or on the Stanley website, but, evidently, they do not make replacement lids for these bottles.  I contacted the Stanley company just to make sure that they do not make a replacement lid (I explained that the lids were broken due to drops, and I was hoping to purchase new lids).  I received an email back stating that all Stanley products are covered under a lifetime warrant, and they then asked me to submit pictures and fill out a detailed form, which I did, though, it took me a long time to compile all of the requested information, and I had to resend the email 4 times as their email kept telling me that it was "undeliverable".  A few days later, I received an email saying that my "ticket" had been resolved and closed, but I had never received a response from my original email.  So, I emailed back stating that my issue was not resolved, and I resent all of the information that they had originally requested.  Weeks later, I received an email apologizing for how busy they are and stating that the warranty doesn't cover accidental damage, and that I should look on their website or Amazon for a replacement lid.  So, basically I just wasted a bunch of time submitting useless information that they never needed and never received an answer to my original questions.  So, that's that.  If you buy this water bottle, just know that if it gets dropped at all, the cheap, plastic lid will break, and you will be left with a very nice, but useless water bottle.

Old Timer Generational USA Series Traditional Fixed and Folding Knives with 1095 HC Stainless Steel Blades, Sawcut Bone Handles, and Made in USA for Hunting, Skinning, EDC, Field Dressing, and Outdoor I have a pocket knife in my pocket at all times and I have found having one on me is almost always useful. I had not heard of Old Timer until recently, but their knives look nice and I thought I would give them a chance. So far I am very pleased with this particular knife.

This is a no-frills knife that doesn't try to get too fancy. The blades have to be pulled open manually without a spring assist, and it does not have some of the things that other knives frequently have such as a corkscrew, screwdriver and other integrated emergency tools. Instead it has three blades - nothing more. Each blade is different and has different uses, though the thought that comes to mind when I look at the knife as a whole is whittling and carving.

The blades are tight and do not wobble. That's a good thing and says that the knife as a whole is assembled well. The blades feel solid and secure when opened.

I love the bone handle. It feels good in the hand and it looks retro which is a good thing. The texture makes it easy to maintain a grip, even when hands are just a little wet.

This is a smallish knife, so it will fit in your pocket and not take up lots of room. This is a little smaller than most knives I am used to carrying, and that's a mixed bag to me - on one hand I like having a larger knife, probably because I am used to having one, but on the other I like the fact that it is small, compact and lightweight.

This is a very nice knife that sticks to getting the basics right without a bunch of extras that only add weight and take away from the overall package. It looks great and is made well.

text_fidelity_a:
KONGDI Desk Exercise Bike Pedal Exerciser Bike Training Green UPDATE:
I have been using this bike since I wrote this review- 5 out of 7 days. I LOVE IT. It helps me so much. It has stayed quiet, easy to use, but really does help me a TON with leg pain that have during the stressful winters at my house.
I am VERY THANKFUL to have this.
----------------------------------------
ORIGINAL REVIEW
I have been wanting an exercise bike for some time now, but we have very little space for anything big. When I saw this, I was hoping it would be what I have needed. Let's take a look.

HOW DOES THIS COME?
This comes in pieces and you have to put it together. It is not easy to do, but if you are patient, it does not take TOO long. The pieces are laid out well and labeled so if you take the time to put them all on the floor as you get ready to assemble, it will be easier in the long run. It comes with all that you need to assemble it including batteries.

ASSEMBLY?
The assembly of this was a bit of a battle for me. I had to put the screws in several times and just as I was getting the pedals into the screw in places, it got really frustrating. There was a black shard of metal that was very hard to see on the threads of the pedal that I was supposed to screw into place. It cut me pretty badly.

While I was bleeding, my husband took his hand, saw what happened and repeated the mistake. He found the shard, and it had been wedged in the threads just right and boy was it sharp. So, be CAREFUL when you assemble. It might be a one time thing, but you never know.

HOW DOES THIS WORK?
This bike pedal machine works GREAT. It is truly silent and smooth running. The pedals are comfortable and with the straps on them hold onto the feed. The mechanism is smooth and it also works very well with only occasional small noises now and then. Other than that, it is close to silent.

MONITOR
The monitor has various settings on it. There is time, speed distance, and calories burned. You can also press the mode button and it will flash from one setting to the other as you pedal.

ON OFF?
The monitor turns off automatically when you stop pedaling and when you start again, it turns on.

ANY PROBLEMS?
The only problem for me is that the monitor is loosely sitting on a piece of metal. On the floor it is fine, but I plan to eventually have a place to hang it up on the wall when not in use. I will have to figure out a way to put the monitor on there a bit more securely so it does not fly off by mistake when hanging or removing. The monitor is held on by a wire.

DOES IT WORK WELL?
I love this thing. Despite our very rocky battle to assemble, it was worth it. I really like this machine. It is helping me a lot already with some muscle/fibro pain. My legs are already getting stronger after only less than a week and about 30 minutes a day of use. I can not tell you how happy I am to have this. I have needed something to get me through the winter and in our small house, it is hard to find anything because of lack of floor space.

THE BOTTOM LINE
If you are careful with this when assembling it is worth the effort. This bike pedal machine works well (I have it on half rug and half floor) and as long as you are on a stable chair, it stays put. I can feel the difference in my body already.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. I am so happy to have this. Believe it or not, it matches my chair perfectly too. It looks like a set!

CAT WHACKER
My cat is fascinated by this machine. She comes and tries to sniff the pedals as I use it and keeps getting whacked in the chin. She does not stop though. When it is turned off, she leaves. When I am using it again, over she comes to be whacked in the chin again! HAHA Cats are weird.
text_fidelity_b: KONGDI Desk Exercise Bike Pedal Exerciser Bike Training Green
